text:
Response A is under the 120-word limit (roughly 100 words) and covers the main items: council works, finances, Clean Up Day, carols, Wattle Road and the next meeting. It has one accuracy slip. It says council "will install" a speed counter, but the minutes say Cr Tse would only ask council traffic staff to put one on Wattle Road and report back. That overstates a conditional commitment. It also omits the Facebook point and the named coordinators, which are minor for a busy manager.

Response B is accurate on the speed counter ("will request") and includes the Facebook item and the names of those responsible. However, it runs to roughly 200 words, well over the 120-word cap. It also wastes words on filler such as "Thank you all for attending" and "kindly provided", which is odd in a summary written for someone who wasn't there. Its added detail is mostly minor, and it breaks an explicit instruction by a wide margin.

On accuracy alone B is slightly better, since A's error is a real overstatement. But A's error is limited to one line, while B fails the core constraint of the request and carries filler that doesn't belong in a manager's summary. A is the more usable response overall.

Verdict: A
